summary: Chijun Hamada is a Buddhist studies scholar attested in 1978 as an assistant at Taisho University and as a researcher at its Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism.

Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at the University of British Columbia (under Karin Preisendanz and Ashok Narhar Aklujkar) and a PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura.
Chiko Corona is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Kenko Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.

Chikyo Yamamoto (1910–1993) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He served at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1970) and later as a part-time lecturer (attested 1980).

Chime Rinpoche (1941–2026) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Gangshar around 1957–1959. He later held a post at the British Library from circa 1965 to 1978.

Chin Kung (1927–2022) was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Chinese Culture University (1975–1980). He later held leadership and honorary professor roles at institutions including Griffith University, the University of Queensland, and Renmin University of China.

Ching Keng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology who earned his PhD from Harvard University (circa 2001–2009) under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. Around 2011, he was an associate professor at National Chengchi University.

Ching-mao Cheng (1933–2025) was a Sinologist and Japanologist who earned his PhD from Princeton (circa 1965–1970). He taught at UC Berkeley, chaired Asian Languages and Literatures at UMass Amherst (circa 1976–1996), and was Founding Chair at National Dong Hwa University.

Ching-mei Shyu is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. She completed an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Jan Nattier and a PhD at Cornell University (awarded 2008) supervised by Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.
Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He founded Silpakorn University, where he served as Director in 1996.

Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyodo Koshuin. He directed the Saijō-ji and Nagano training monasteries, served as abbot at Sōji-ji (circa 1944–1967), and founded Tsurumi Women's University in 1966.
Chishō Namai (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He served at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1996) and later as president (attested 2008).

Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed a master's degree at Kyoto University (circa 1966–1968). He held posts as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (1979–1983) and professor at Tokoha University (1989).

Chizen Akanuma (1884–1937) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Otani University and Kōkōdō under Manshi Kiyozawa. He became a professor at Otani University in 1919 and co-founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921.

Chizuko Yoshimizu (born 1959), a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, earned a doctorate from the University of Vienna (1994). She advanced from lecturer to professor at the University of Tsukuba (2003–2011) and joined Toyo Bunko in 2019.
Chlodwig H. Werba (born 1957) is a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna, attested between 1997 and 2022.
Chogye Shabdrung (born 1981) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso and attended Sakya College in 2003.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Kunga Chöphel, Geshe Tshechok, and Zimwok Rinpoche. In 1928, he became the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Phenpo Nalendra Monastery.
Chogyu Takayama (1871–1902) was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied at Fukushima Prefectural Asaka High School and the University of Tokyo (circa 1893–1896).
Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa (1829–1870) was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé.
